content.overview: BNS s. 167 — Persons subject to certain Acts.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Persons subject to certain Acts. BNS restatement of IPC 139. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 139. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 167 is the rule on “Persons subject to certain Acts”. The section provides that no person subject to the Air Force Act, 1950, the Army Act, 1950 and the Navy Act, 1957, or shall be subject to punishment under this Sanhita for any of the offences defined in this Chapter. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 167 exists so that “Persons subject to certain Acts” has a closed legal test in Chapter VIII — Of Offences Relating to the Army, Navy and Air Force. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Mutiny, desertion, insubordination, and wearing a service garb.

The provision in detail
167. No person subject to the Air Force Act, 1950, the Army Act, 1950 and the Navy Act, 1957, or shall be subject to punishment under this Sanhita for any of the offences defined in this Chapter
